summary: Mission Viejo holds the distinction of being one of the largest master-planned communities ever built in the United States — nearly all 18 square miles of it were designed as a single development starting in the 1960s, which explains why the street grid, park system, and commercial nodes feel unusually coordinated rather than piecemeal. That planning shows in the trail network threading through rolling South Orange County hills, connecting neighborhoods to a man-made lake — Lake Mission Viejo — that functions as a private recreational hub with a sandy beach, an oddity this far inland. The terrain is genuinely hilly, carved by the upper Oso Creek watershed, and western-facing homes catch Pacific-tinged sunsets over the Saddleback Valley ridgeline. With average daily highs around 74°F and over nine hours of sunshine year-round, outdoor routines are nearly weatherproof. Economically, this is primarily a bedroom community; most employment gravity pulls toward Irvine's tech and medical-device corridor or the healthcare campuses clustered near Mission Hospital, and I-5 commutes define the rhythm. A median home value near $946,000 against a median household income of roughly $136,000 yields a price-to-income ratio around 7:1 — comfortable by coastal Orange County standards, though still steep enough that renting at $2,713 per month absorbs a meaningful share of even that median income. Property crime sits around 1,239 per 100K, dominated heavily by larceny rather than burglary or vehicle theft. The essential tension: extraordinary physical infrastructure and connectivity within the city, paired with deep financial dependence on employment centers you have to drive to reach.
